General Amherlt with a body of 12,000 men was commanded to attack Crown Point; General Wolfe was to undertake the fiege of Quebec; while general Prideaux and Sir William Johnlon were to attempt a French fort near the cataracts of Niagara. This left expedition was the first that fucceeded. The fiege was begun with vigour, and promised an early conquelt; but general Prideaux was killed in the trenches by the burling of a mortar, fo that the whole command devolved on general John-fon. A body of French troops, fentile of the importance of the place, attempted to relieve it; but were utterly defeated and difperfed; foon after which, the garrifon furrendered prifoners of war. On his arrival at the forts of Crown Point and Ticonderago, general Amherk found them deferted and destroyed. There now remained, therefore, but one decisive blow to reduce all North America under the British dominion; and this was by the taking of Quebec the capital of Canada. This expedition was commanded by admiral Saunders and general Wolfe.
